judged_text: ZAddGuestsInputSchema enforces only per-string email format with no uniqueness, and the handler's filter (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78) only exact-matches existing attendees, so duplicate or case-variant emails create duplicate Attendee rows. Adding 'John@X.com' when attendee 'john@x.com' already exists — reachable through the dialog, whose uniqueness check only covers the input array — persists a second attendee row for the same person who then receives two different guest emails; a direct API caller can pass the same email twice for the same result.

adjudication.rationale: The server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness or normalization. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering out emails that exactly match existing attendee emails (`guest === attendee.email`) and blacklisted entries, but it does not (a) lower-case/normalize emails for comparison, nor (b) dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. Therefore, a direct API caller can submit the same email twice and both entries can reach `createMany`, and a case-variant like `John@x.com` will not be filtered out if an existing attendee is `john@x.com` (exact match check), potentially creating duplicate attendee rows. The UI dialog’s local uniqueness check also only de-dupes within the input array and is case-sensitive, so case-variant duplicates remain reachable via the dialog.
